sense: of a person: a name of rank or honour

terms.comment: A calling by name, and so the name or title one is called by. Its other classical senses are an address to someone and, in law, an appeal (to the tribunes, Cic. Quinct. 64).

evidence: Cic. Pis. 19: sustinēre titulum cōnsulātūs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A title as a mark of honour (titulus cōnsulātūs), not a form of address; also the title of a book (see title, of a book).

phrases.latin: vēnit interim Bibulus; crēdō, voluit appellātiōne hāc inānī nōbīs esse pār.
phrases.english: Meanwhile Bibulus arrived; I suppose he wanted to be my equal in this empty title.
